transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07
Start time: 10:00am PT
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Nina Gomez (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Redwood Channel Dir), Liam O'Connor (Zephyr Channel Manager), Hannah Lee (Zephyr AE), Marco Diaz (Zephyr Solutions Architect)
Links shared: joint-pipeline.xlsx (drive link), redwood-partner-playbook.pdf (link), perf-benchmarks (sheet link)

Summary:
- Quick run through joint pipeline: focus on Acme (P0), Nova Retail (P1), Orion Logistics (P2)
- Agreed to run a short perf/cost estimation for Acme POC and align on partner discount tiers
- Need procurement intro from Zephyr to Acme; schedule technical deep dive next week

Topics:
- Pipeline health and stages (commitments, blockages)
- Technical blocker review for Acme POC (latency SLOs, model size, data residency)
- Commercial alignment (discounts, split, logos, who owns procurement ask)
- Next steps and owner assignment

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: ok uh thanks everyone for hopping on, I know we have a tight agenda so we'll run through the joint pipe, call out blockers, and agree next steps
[00:18] Liam: yeah thanks Samir quick note first we updated the sheet with two new leads from last week, Acme moved to legal review so that's our main one
[00:35] Nina: quick q on Acme, what model sizes did they say again, is it mostly 7B or they leaning 13B plus
[00:50] Hannah: I think they started with 7b but last convo they mentioned some generative summarize use that might push to 13b, Marco you can correct me
[01:05] Marco: yeah the initial prod tests were 7b but their QA team said they want parity with current in-house results so 13 to 20b for accuracy, um there's also data residency constraint, they want EU-only for some flows
[01:30] Aisha: okay that's important for us, reminds me we should call out Private deployment options and VPC flow, we can offer Redwood Private for the EU subset
[01:50] Samir: right, and just to be clear on cost tradeoffs, running 13b on Dedicated will change economics, but we have quantized variants and batching options to bring cost down; Nina can share rough numbers
[02:10] Nina: yeah I'll do a quick estimate, but we should flag that if they want sub-100ms p99 we may need dedicated capacity for parts of the workload, otherwise hosted with aggressive caching might be fine
[02:35] Liam: on the commercial side, where does Zephyr fit in, do we open a co-sell deal or are we doing referral and Zephyr leads procurement
[02:50] Hannah: we usually prefer co-sell with shared SLAs, Zephyr would own the client relationship but share uplift, Samir thoughts
[03:05] Samir: co-sell works, we need clear rules on pricing tiers and logo rights; Aisha can outline partner discount tiers
[03:20] Aisha: yes we have standard partner tiers, I'll send the playbook but for this class of deal probably Tier 2 discount, and if they commit to a 12mo reserved Dedicated we can bump it
[03:40] Marco: minor point on infra, their infra team uses GCP europe-west6 primarily, any region-specific capacity constraints on Redwood side
[03:55] Nina: we have dedicated pools in europe-west and can spin private nodes in that region, there is some lead time but the Dedicated team can provision within 2-3 weeks if commit
[04:15] Liam: perfect that matches their timeline, procurement expects vendor selection by end of July so provisioning lead time is tight
[04:30] Samir: ok then we should prioritize getting them a perf estimate and pricing so they can move to procurement, action items there
[04:45] Hannah: any security questions we should pre-empt, Acme is pretty strict on SOC2, SSO and audit logs
[05:00] Nina: we support SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS integration and can provide SOC2 report, though for Private deployments they'd likely want on-prem or customer-controlled KMS
[05:20] Marco: can you give a quick sense on audit log retention and how easy it is to pull logs for compliance audits
[05:35] Aisha: we can provide tailorable retention windows and exportable audit logs, I'll link our compliance pack after the call
[05:50] Samir: good, ok shifting back to pipeline review, let's go row-by-row on the shared sheet, Acme first, then Nova, Orion, and a couple smaller deals at the end
[06:05] Liam: Acme - currently committed to pilot, procurement stage, estimated ARR 600k, stakeholders: CTO (Jared), Head of AI (Priya), procurement lead (Meera)
[06:25] Nina: any defined success metrics for the pilot
[06:35] Hannah: they want latency p95 < 200ms for chat UI and embed throughput for search, also cost-per-call targets, they need to validate hallucination rate is below threshold
[06:50] Nina: hallucination metric, ok we can pair on evals and share our quality baseline, and we can run a small quantization test to see quality vs size tradeoff
[07:10] Samir: timeline wise they want pilot in mid-July, which is tight but doable if we get procurement intro this week and we have the perf numbers by next Monday
[07:30] Marco: I'm concerned about the EU-only flow, will that complicate shared caching or cross-region fallbacks
[07:45] Nina: it does add a constraint, we can route EU traffic to a Private cluster in europe-west and keep other traffic on hosted, routing policies will handle it, though it adds ops overhead for them
[08:05] Liam: on comp mentions Acme's procurement asked about alternative vendors, they named Anthropic and Bedrock in the RFP, how do we position vs them
[08:20] Samir: we should lead with predictable inference unit economics, transparent benchmarking, and our routing/fallback story; also show the Dedicated/private option for data residency
[08:35] Hannah: Zephyr can emphasize our faster onboarding and lower engineering lift vs self-hosting
[08:45] Aisha: also stress our tooling like per-route tracing and cost breakdowns, that's resonated with other retailers
[09:00] Samir: great, moving to Nova Retail, status is discovery, they are evaluating embeddings for recommendation, estimated ARR 150k
[09:15] Marco: question on embeddings cost model, does Redwood charge per vector or per-request
[09:25] Nina: per-embedding unit today, and we have volume discounts and caching for repeated vectors, we'll include details in the sheet
[09:40] Liam: Nova asked about latency tolerances, they can tolerate higher p95 for batch jobs, less so for real-time
[09:50] Samir: good candidate for hosted + caching there, lower barrier to entry, smaller proof to show ROI
[10:05] Hannah: quick ask, can Redwood support a short 24h benchmark run against their real queries so Nova can see real numbers
[10:20] Nina: yes we'll run a workload run, need a sample trace and model choice, if it's 7b we can run on hosted, if 13b we'll need reserved capacity for consistent p99
[10:40] Samir: note for the record, we should capture who will provide sample traces - Zephyr to collect from Nova and upload to shared drive
[10:55] Liam: yes will do, Hannah will coordinate
[11:05] Samir: ok Orion Logistics next, longer sales cycle, flagged as P2, lower priority this quarter
[11:20] Marco: they asked about private on-prem options because of regulated supply chain data
[11:30] Aisha: Private/on-prem is an option but requires longer procurement and legal, we should table it for now unless they accelerate
[11:45] Samir: quick pause, any blockers on Redwood side to run Acme perf test this week
[11:55] Nina: need model weights (or a representative subset) and sample traffic, and confirmation of EU-only subset; otherwise we can run synthetic traces but results will be approximate
[12:15] Hannah: procurement intro is the blocker on their side, Liam can you escalate
[12:25] Liam: will do, I'll ask for an intro to Meera and copy Samir
[12:40] Samir: commercial question - for Acme if they want a 12mo committed Dedicated we can do a deeper partner margin, do Zephyr have preferred split models
[12:55] Hannah: we typically do 70/30 in favor of partner on direct-sourced deals but open to discuss on bigger commitments
[13:10] Samir: sounds fine, we'll propose a structure in the sheet, and legal can draft a co-sell addendum if they move to signature
[13:25] Aisha: also reminder about logos and case study approval workflow, need to confirm if Acme will allow public case study
[13:40] Marco: they said internal comms only for now, might allow public after 6 months
[13:55] Samir: ok near the end here - wanted to surface a tech concern we saw in a separate POC, the KV cash management had some blowups with warmup spikes
[14:10] Nina: yeah I think you mean KV cache, and we saw the warm startup latency in one of our older kernels, we patched it - current runtime handles warmups better but we'll include guidance on warm start strategies
[14:30] Liam: perfect call that out, Acme will want assurance there
[14:45] Samir: shall we recap actions and owners
[15:00] Hannah: quick recap: Zephyr will intro procurement, Zephyr will collect sample traces, Redwood will run perf and share numbers, Samir will update pipeline and propose pricing tiers
[15:20] Nina: and I'll include quantization and batch recs plus notes on p99 vs p95 tradeoffs
[15:35] Samir: any other questions, folks
[15:40] Liam: none from me, thanks everyone
[15:45] Samir: thanks all, we'll send the updated pipeline and schedule deep dive once we have Meera's intro

End of transcript.
